findings.title: Case-sensitive BlockedEmail lookup allows bypassing email blocks with uppercase characters
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` queries `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` without normalizing the input email's case (e.g., via `Email.downcase(email)`), and `BlockedEmail` does not normalize `email` before saving or validating uniqueness. Because `User` validates `email` before downcasing it (or accepts mixed-case emails in `User.new_from_params`), a user can bypass a blocked entry for `bad@spammers.org` simply by signing up with `Bad@spammers.org`.

findings.title: Validation runs twice during user creation, double-counting blocked email matches
findings.body: In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` is called on line 168 (when `SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` is enabled) and then `user.save` runs validations a second time on line 172. Because `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and saves the record as a side effect of validation, any signup attempt with a tracked email (for instance one configured with `:do_nothing`, or whenever `valid?` is called before `save`) will increment `match_count` multiple times for a single signup attempt.
